outcome: Externalizing behaviors (measured by Infant-Toddler Social and Emotional Assessment)
cohort: The study included 94 healthy term-born control neonates and 94 preterm infants, with a subset of 30 preterm infants followed up for behavioral assessment.
finding: CAN connectivity was significantly higher in term neonates compared to preterm neonates at term-equivalent age, with connectivity in preterm neonates positively correlating with PMA and negatively correlating with externalizing behaviors at 18-month follow-up.
